method: 5 msgs per size at gap 5000 ms via spotter_tx; Spotter console captured on Mac USB (b1_console_capture.txt); post between steps

probe_S09B0.console: Added to MS_Q_CELLULAR_ONLY (1); Sending Cellular message to Notecard ~40 ms after add — small messages drain immediately

1100.error: BM Binary Cellular message too large: 1100 bytes

1200.error: BM Binary Cellular message too large: 1200 bytes

findings: Payload ceiling is exactly 1000 B (1001 wire len incl. null accepted; 1100 rejected pre-queue). Matches bm_core spotter_tx_max_cellular_payload_bytes 1000.
0x02 maps to MS_Q_CELLULAR_ONLY on Spotter fw v2.16.6 — repo network-type bytes confirmed; forum t/575 'type 2 does not exist' does not apply here.

At ~1 kB payloads, messages batch-drain: drain task ran ~10.8 s after first add in every burst, then handed messages to Notecard at ~1.3 s/msg. Max 2 pending between drains — the 3rd message in each burst was dropped (Queue ... is full), silently from the Pi's perspective.
Small messages (427 B probe; Spotter's own 6129 B internal message) drained ~instantly — drain behavior is size-dependent (or queue-empty-dependent).

CONSEQUENCE: at 1 kB, gap 5000 ms is ALREADY lossy (4/5 delivered). The spec's B2 sweep (5000->250 ms) assumed the floor was below 5 s; it is at-or-above. B2 adjusted to a (size x gap) matrix to find bytes/s optimum.

quota_spend_payload_bytes.note: size-rejected and queue-dropped messages never reached the Notecard
